help_detail:
Use the Co-author builder (button below this field) to add authors one at a time as separate First / Middle / Last parts, rather than typing the whole list by hand. It formats and joins the names consistently and avoids the delimiter ambiguity described below.

HANDLING UNUSUAL NAMES

Suffixes (Jr., Sr., II, III, IV): there is no separate suffix box. Put the suffix at the end of the Last name field, e.g. Last name = "Smith Jr." or "Williams III". Do not put it in Middle name -- the "Last, First Middle" and "Last, Initials" formats place Middle after the comma, after the given names, so a suffix there reads oddly ("Smith, John Jr." becomes "Smith, Jr. John").

Compound or two-part surnames (e.g. "Lopez Lopez", Spanish paternal+maternal surnames, "Garcia Martinez"): type the full compound as one Last name, e.g. Last name = "Lopez Lopez". Do not split it across Last and Middle -- Middle is for an actual middle name or initial, and splitting a compound surname there will misformat it and will also be parsed incorrectly later if you use "Reformat existing text".

Surname particles (e.g. "van der Berg", "de la Cruz", "von Neumann"): include the particle with the surname in the Last name box, following the author's own preferred capitalization, e.g. "van der Berg".

Hyphenated surnames (e.g. "Garcia-Lopez"): enter as one Last name with the hyphen, no surrounding spaces.

A single-name author (no distinct given/family name): put the full name in Last name and leave First and Middle blank.

TYPING THE FIELD DIRECTLY (without the builder)

Separate authors with commas by default. This is safe for plain "First Last" names.

If any name is written "Last, First" or "Last, Initials" style, it already contains a comma, so comma-separating the author list becomes ambiguous ("Lopez Lopez, J., Smith, A." could be read as four authors instead of two). Use semicolons between authors instead: "Lopez Lopez, J.; Smith, A."

The builder's "Reformat existing text" button re-splits the current field text on whatever delimiter you select and reloads it as editable rows -- always review the result for unusual names (compound surnames, suffixes, particles) before re-applying, since the automatic parser only recognizes simple "First [Middle] Last" or "Last, First Middle" shapes and does not special-case any of the above.

Open license for the free e-book
help_detail: Open licenses, from least to most restrictive: CC BY (attribution only); CC BY-SA (attribution plus share-alike); CC BY-NC (non-commercial); CC BY-NC-SA (non-commercial plus share-alike); CC0 (public domain dedication, no rights reserved); All Rights Reserved (not actually open; use only if required by a co-publisher). For a free online course text, CC BY or CC BY-NC are the most common choices. CC BY lets anyone reuse and adapt your material, even commercially, as long as they credit you; CC BY-NC removes the commercial-reuse permission if that matters to you.
